Welcome to Emmanuel Church of England Primary School
Our School
Emmanuel Church
Emmanuel Church
Emmanuel Church enjoys a warm and collaborative relationship with the School in the service of the whole wider community of West Hampstead. Church of England Schools are not “faith schools” in the way that such phrases are often used in the media and elsewhere, but rather schools which exist for the whole community. At Emmanuel Church we would see ourselves as generously orthodox and everyone is warmly welcome at all our services and activities, irrespective of race, age, way of life, sexual orientation or physical ability.
We are members of the umbrella network “Inclusive Church” and would see the essential inclusivity of the Gospel of Jesus Christ as central to our core values.
Sunday Services at Emmanuel Church include:
8am - Eucharist (said)
A quiet reflective service to start the Lord’s day lasting about 30 minutes.
9.15am - ‘Joyful Noise Eucharist’
A service especially with young, pre-school age children in mind and lasting 35 to 40 minutes
10.30 am - Sung Eucharist
Our more traditional, choral service.
Children’s Church (Sunday School) meets during this service during term-time
Each week the whole school attends Church for a celebration of the Eucharist and are often joined by parents, friends and members of the community. As a Christian school, our inclusive Christian values permeate our curriculum and assemblies and parents and carers are asked to accept this when they send their children to Emmanuel School.
This essential inclusivity ensures that we are not doctrinaire or inappropriately proselytising. It is the right of every parent or carer to withdraw their child from acts of worship if they so wish. We rejoice that we live in a diverse and multicultural society, and it is the policy of the school to teach children about other beliefs and traditions to enable them to be sensitive and tolerant towards those whose religion and culture is different from their own.

Welcome to Emmanuel Church of England Primary School
Our School
Collective Worship
Collective Worship
Collective worship is a sacred and significant time of each school day, where we gather together as a whole school family. Collective worship strengthens and supports the Christian identity of our school and reaffirms our Christian vision and associated values of respect, service, wisdom, joy, forgiveness and resilience.
At Emmanuel we have a daily act of collective worship which is held as a whole school. Once a week, this is held in Emmanuel Church.
In our school we have, as a thread running through our work, the belief and practice of the Christian church. Christian beliefs about God, Jesus and the Church are explored through stories and discussion in classes.
During the school year we celebrate Christian festivals and other important events in the school calendar.
Our Collective Worships are important times when children come together to enjoy stories and songs and to reflect on religious, spiritual, moral and social issues. They are inclusive, invitational and inspirational and are theologically routed in the stories from the New Testament and Old Testament.
At Emmanuel, we recognise that our Collective Worship should provide the opportunity for pupils and adults to be included whilst allowing the freedom of those of different faiths and those who profess no religious faith to be present and to engage with integrity.
In our Friday Celebration Worship we celebrate children’s successes by presenting Headteacher Awards and Visionary awards, for living out our school vision. They all receive a big clap and are mentioned in our weekly newsletter!

pageCache.text:
Welcome to Emmanuel Church of England Primary School
Our School
Emmanuel School Vision and Values
Emmanuel School Vision and Values
Jesus said, "I have come that they may have life, life in all its fullness" (John 10:10). This reflects a life of purpose found in relationship with God, where each child is nurtured and given the opportunities to reach their full potential.
Jesus identifies Himself as the Alpha and the Omega, the beginning and the end. "From Alpha to Omega" reflects our goal for our children to experience "life in all its fullness" throughout their educational journey; preparing them to flourish in an ever-changing, diverse world.
We aspire for everyone in our school community to grow into life in all its fullness: academically, spiritually, physically, emotionally, morally and socially. By nurturing growth in these areas, we empower students to reach their fullest potential and live lives shaped by the values of respect, service, wisdom, resilience, forgiveness and joy.
Theological foundation of ‘Life in all its fullness’
The theological foundation of "life in all its fullness" is rooted in the teachings of Jesus Christ, particularly in the story of the Good Shepherd (John 10:11-18).
Jesus, as the Good Shepherd, offers His life for the sheep, guiding them with care and providing for their every need. He promises that His followers will experience abundant life, not just in quantity but in quality—through His love, protection, and guidance. Just as the Good Shepherd nurtures and cares for each of His sheep, we believe that through faith in Christ, every individual can flourish and experience the fullness of life He offers, living with love, grace, and purpose.
We are a Voluntary Aided Church of England Primary School, at the heart of the vibrant community of West Hampstead, providing an education for children between 3 and 11 years. Following the best aspirations of the original founders of Church of England schools, we are an inclusive school community in the Christian tradition, which rejoices in diversity, serving the whole wider community.
Our school is situated in a beautiful new building (the Omega building) opened in November 2012. The original Victorian building at 101 Mill Lane (the Alpha building) has recently been refurbished to create an open-plan Early Years’ Foundation Stage Unit.
We warmly encourage you to browse through this website to discover all that we can offer your child.
Our six school values are:
“Do to others what you would have them do to you.”
Be joyful always, pray continually, give thanks in all circumstances, for this is God’s will for you in Christ Jesus.”
Thessalonians 5:16-18
“All wisdom comes from God.”
“Forgive us for doing wrong, as we forgive others.”
“Now that I, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also should wash one another’s feet."
“So let us not grow weary in doing what is right, for we will reap at harvest time, if we do not give up.”
Please visit Emmanuel Church’s website here: https://www.emmanuelnw6.com/

Welcome to Emmanuel Church of England Primary School
Our School
Partnership
Partnership
In September 2023, the Governors made successful appointments to the leadership of Emmanuel School and agreed on a strategic partnership with two other Camden Church of England Schools – Hampstead Parochial and Holy Trinity NW3.
Emmanuel’s Head of School is Kate Roscoe. Miss Roscoe was formerly the acting Head of School at Hampstead Parochial. She has a strong track record in teaching and learning and a great passion for music and drama. Kate shares with Emmanuel’s Governors a clear sense of how our school’s Christian vision – ‘Life in all its fullness’ – balances strong aspiration with a commitment to giving our children a broad grounding for their future. Kate will provide day-to-day leadership and will act as an ambassador for Emmanuel at the school gates and a role model inside the school.
The new three-school partnership is led by Laura Hall as Executive Headteacher. Mrs Hall led Hampstead Parochial and Holy Trinity into partnership two years ago and has begun to deliver the benefits available to schools who invest thoughtfully in greater collaboration. Laura has done so whilst protecting the individual and ‘small school’ ethos of three very different schools, each of which is much loved by its local community.

Welcome to Emmanuel Church of England Primary School
Our School
Wraparound Care
Wraparound Care
At Emmanuel, we offer an extended wraparound provision between the hours of 8am-5:30pm.
We are able to do this by offering a Breakfast Club and a daily After School Club called 'The Den' in our Alpha Building.
Our breakfast club runs from 8am until the start of the school day, Monday to Friday, and is available to the whole school (Nursery-Year 6).
Children will be provided with a healthy and nutritious breakfast and a selection of games and arts & crafts are available for the second half of each session.
Places are allocated on a first come, first served basis; children are not automatically entitled to a place because they have attended the club previously. We have a limited number of places, so we urge everyone to book in advance.
The cost of Breakfast Club is currently £4 per day.
Emmanuel's after-school club, AKA ‘The Den’, runs from the end of the school day until 5:30pm, Monday-Friday, and is available to the whole school (Nursery-Year 6).
Families can request to book either the full 2-hour session from 3.30pm-5.30pm or a 1-hour session which runs from 4.30pm-5.30pm. In both instances, children can be collected at any time but must be collected by 5:30pm at the very latest.
Children attending Emmanuel activity clubs can book the 4.30-5.30pm session and a member of staff will collect children from their clubs and take them to 'The Den'.
The club will be staffed by Rising Stars who are specialists in wraparound care for children. 'The Den' will very much be moulded around the children attending as we strive to give it a real home-from-home feel. It will include games, activities, arts & crafts, music, reading corner and outdoor play in the Alpha playground.
The cost of joining 'The Den' is currently as follows:
3:30-5:30pm - £15 per day
4:30-5:30pm - £7.50 per day
